question: Your name, your business name, your website.
Where you're located (city, state) and your time zone.
Who is on camera?
guidance: You, a partner, an employee, your kids, your spouse, nobody. Be specific about who is willing to be filmed and who is off limits.

question: Fill in the sentence.
guidance: We help [who] get [what result] without [what they hate].

question: What stage are you at?
guidance: One line. Revenue per month (a range is fine), months in business, customers so far.

question: Every product you sell.
guidance: For each one: the name, the price written as $X.XX, the page it lives on, and one sentence in this shape. "It delivers [solution] for [who], from [their struggle] to [the outcome], so they can [the benefit]."

question: Your best seller, and why you think it's the best seller.
Bundles, kits, or multi-packs, with prices.
Free shipping threshold, if any.
Guarantee, trial, or return policy, in the exact words you use on your site.
Anything you give away for free.
guidance: A guide, a sample, a template. What it's called, where it lives, what it's for.

question: The ONE thing you want these videos to sell.
guidance: Pick one. If every video points at a different thing, none of them work.

question: Where the call to action goes.
guidance: Link in bio, a specific page, a comment keyword, a DM. If you use a keyword tool like ManyChat, list every keyword you have live and what it sends.

question: What is physically true about the product.
guidance: Materials, ingredients, dimensions, sizes, colors, weights.

question: What it does that the alternatives don't.
guidance: Plain words. No adjectives.

question: What it does NOT do.
guidance: Every limit you know about. Where it doesn't work, who it doesn't fit, what it can't handle.

question: Claims you can and cannot make on camera.
guidance: Patent, patent pending, food safe, non-toxic, made in, tested by, lasts X months, guaranteed. Write "yes, can say" or "no, don't say" next to each one.

question: Numbers you ARE willing to say out loud.
guidance: Units sold, years in business, review count and rating, retail stores you're in, money spent on R&D, batches tested, customers served. Only the ones you'd say on camera to a stranger.

question: Numbers you are NOT willing to say out loud.
guidance: So the tool never uses them.

question: Where it's made, by whom, and whether that's part of the story.
Words and phrases you cannot say on camera, or hate hearing.
guidance: Anything you stumble on, any industry acronym, any word that isn't you. One founder can't say "EIN" and says "tax ID number" instead. Write yours down.

question: Paste at least 20 reviews, raw, with the star rating.
guidance: Paste reviews here. Unedited is better than polished. Include the bad ones.

question: Customer emails, DMs, or comments that made you feel something.
guidance: Paste the ones you screenshotted.

question: Any customer interviews, surveys, or research.
guidance: If a consultant wrote you a report, paste the whole report.

question: How do customers describe your product to their friends?
guidance: If you've heard it said out loud, write it exactly how they said it.

question: What is the moment a customer decides to buy? What just happened to them?
guidance: Examples: a kid came home with another hole in his knee. The third pair of $40 pants went in the trash this month. They were standing in a store aisle doing math.

question: What did they try before you, and why did each one fail?
guidance: Every alternative, brand, workaround, and DIY fix you've heard of.

question: What almost stopped them from buying?
guidance: Every objection, in their words. Price, sizing, "will it actually work," "is it gimmicky," "I've been burned before."

question: What surprised them after they bought?
guidance: The thing they didn't expect.

question: What did the kid say? The spouse? The friend?
guidance: Anything a third party said about the product that a customer repeated to you.

question: Describe your best customer as one specific person.
guidance: Age, where they live, what they do all day, what they buy, what they're tired of. Give them a name if it helps.

question: Their top three pain points, in order, in the words they'd use.
The dream result.
guidance: What life looks like when the problem is gone. Not "peace of mind." The actual scene.

question: What have they given up on?
guidance: The thing they stopped expecting to ever get fixed.

question: Any second or third customer type that's meaningfully different.
guidance: The gift buyer, the wholesale buyer, the parent of a picky kid. Same four questions for each.

question: Where are they today?
guidance: Pick one and say why. Most have never heard of your category. Most know the category and are comparing options. Most already know you.

question: Why you started.
guidance: The exact moment, not the summary.

question: The first version that didn't work, and what you changed.
A mistake that cost you money, and what it cost.
A win you didn't expect.
Something a customer did with the product that you never planned for.
A time a big company, a retailer, or an expert told you no.
Something funny that happened.
A moment with your kid, spouse, parent, or friend that involved the product.
The name of your business and where it came from.
Five fun facts about you that have nothing to do with the business.
Three myths in your category that you find yourself correcting.
guidance: For each, the myth and the truth.

question: Three mistakes beginners make, and why it costs them.
Three things about how your product is made, tested, or shipped that a customer would find interesting.
The one question you get asked more than any other.
The question you wish people asked.
Record yourself for two minutes talking about your product to a friend, unscripted. Paste the transcript here.
guidance: Paste the transcript. Don't clean it up. Any voice memo app will transcribe it.

question: Answer these five in writing, the way you'd say them out loud, not the way you'd write them for a website.
Something about your product or your customers you're passionate about.
Why should someone choose you over the alternatives?
A common misconception, explained to someone who believes it.
A recent win, challenge, or funny story, told to a friend.
"So what do you do?" at a party.
Three words for how you want to come across, and three you never want to sound like.
Do you curse on camera?
guidance: A little, never, or freely.

question: How do you naturally end a video?
guidance: A hard call to action, a soft one, a question to the audience, or just stopping on the last line.

question: Past tense or present tense?
guidance: "When I started" or "here's what happens when you." Or either.

question: Paste three sentences from your own videos or posts that sound the most like you.
Every platform you post on, with the handle and the link.
Your three best videos.
guidance: Link, views, comments, and one line on why you think it worked.

question: Your three worst videos that you thought would work.
guidance: Link and one line on what you think happened.

question: Any video that got a lot of comments, even with low views.
guidance: Link and what the comments were about.

question: Paste the transcript of your single best video.
Three creators you like in or near your space.
guidance: Links and why.

question: Three competitors.
guidance: Links. What they do better than you, and what you do better than them.

question: Formats you've tried, and which felt natural versus fake.
guidance: Talking head, voiceover over footage, comparison, tutorial, story, skit, unboxing.

question: What footage you already have.
guidance: Product close-ups, the making of it, shipping, customers using it, kids, family, the workspace, before and afters, fails. Be honest about what's on a hard drive versus what you'd have to shoot.

question: Where you can film.
guidance: Home, workspace, warehouse, outside, a store.

question: Hard limits.
guidance: No kids on camera, no home, no employees, no customers, no public, no acting, no trends. Every limit removes formats, so only list the real ones.

question: How much time you can give to recording per week, honestly.
Do you edit, or does someone else? What tools?
Topics, words, angles, or stories that are off limits.
guidance: Politics, religion, competitors by name, family details, health claims, past business partners, anything.

question: Angles that have backfired.
guidance: If you've ever run a message and it made customers feel bad, guilty, or defensive, describe it so it's never used again.

question: Anything sensitive about the business right now that should not come up.
guidance: A lawsuit, a supplier issue, a recall, a partner dispute.

question: Your selling seasons, in order of importance, with the dates content needs to go live to hit them.
guidance: Holiday content goes out eight weeks early, not the week of.

question: Anything launching in the next 90 days.
Anything going out of stock or being discontinued in the next 90 days.
The constraint your assessment named.
The One Thing you were told to do.
Where you are on it.
How many scripts?
guidance: Default is 20, four per awareness level.

question: Length?
guidance: Under 30 seconds, 30 to 45, or up to 60.

question: Voiceover over footage, talking to camera, or a mix?
Every script can come with a call to action version and a no-call-to-action version. Do you want both, or one?
Anything else the writer should know that isn't in here.
